summary: Mono forest and Grazing Service lookout on Peavine Mountain near Reno, opened 1942; closed 1970 by smog per one paper; no longer standing, removal date unknown.

facts.design: Standard 14-by-14-foot lookout building with sleeping quarters, on a lookout tower
facts.status_note: The 2012 report says it is no longer standing and does not know when it was removed. A 1970 newspaper item reports closure for smog.
facts.agency: Mono National Forest with the U.S. Grazing Service (1942); the Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest stewards the mountain today

access.note: Many miles of hiking and mountain bike trails have been added under Humboldt-Toiyabe stewardship; access from northwest Reno has become more restricted

visit.trail_note: A road winds up the north and east faces to the radio sites on the summit

events.note: Grazing Service crews built the station house and lookout tower; the Forest Service supplied the 14-by-14-foot building, which came from a Susanville site; a five-mile road was built to the summit
Station placed in operation July 21, 1942, with J.P. Ryan of the Mono forest service assigned to the post
Reno Evening Gazette item names Mrs. Jean Ferguson of Carson City as the person running the station
2012 report gives 1964 as the year the lookout was abandoned; the 1970 closure item does not agree
Nevada State Journal reports that smog forced the closure of the lookout
Still standing in 1972, according to the 2012 report

corrections.why: The Forest Fire Lookout Association's Nevada list places Peavine Peak in Washoe County at 39.58694, -119.93194. The brief's point is far from Reno.
The 1942 to 1970 items describe a 14-by-14-foot building and a tower but give no tower height, so the 30.5 m figure has no source.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1942 newspaper items credit the Mono National Forest and the Grazing Service. The 2012 report says the Tahoe National Forest built it originally. The record follows the 1942 items, which are contemporary, and notes the 2012 report's different claim.
The 1970 newspaper item reports closure for smog. The 2012 report gives 1964 for abandonment and 1972 for still standing. The record keeps both and does not choose between them.

notes_for_editor: Probable duplicate of us-nv-peavine-peak: same summit lookout, same 1942 sources, both marked gone; merge candidate. The brief's coordinates are wrong (see corrections). The brief's 30.5 m height has no source. The 1964 abandonment date (2012 report) conflicts with the 1970 closure item and was not reconciled. No source describes the site's remains today beyond radio towers on the summit.
